styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Gold churches, colonial streets and Andean markets.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Volcano views, cloud forest and the high páramo.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Market lunches, ceviche and strong highland coffee.

stays.why: Walk to the churches, plazas and museums. Quiet at night; car-free on Sundays. Many hostels and small hotels.
Backpacker and nightlife zone with the most restaurants and tour agencies. Metro stop nearby.
Modern, safe and green next to the big park and malls. Good for families and business trips.
Local, bohemian neighbourhood with cafés and food spots. Between the old town and the park.

food: Try locro de papa (potato and cheese soup), hornado (roast pork) and llapingachos (cheese potato patties).
Set lunches (almuerzos) at small restaurants cost about $3–5: soup, main and juice. Great value.
Visit a market: Mercado Central or San Francisco for fruit, juices and cheap local plates.
Ceviche and seafood are good; highland trout is a common dish. Wash it down with canelazo (hot spiced drink).
Coffee is a local pride. Look for small specialty cafés in La Floresta and La Mariscal.
more_time: Add a day for the TelefériQo cable car and a short walk on the Pichincha slopes. Go early; clouds build by midday.
Swap a city afternoon for Mitad del Mundo and the Intiñan site on the equator, about an hour north.
Take a day trip to Cotopaxi National Park for volcano views and páramo walks. Book a tour; altitude is high.

recommend.why: Two nights cover the old town and the cable car; add a night for a Cotopaxi or equator day trip.

month_notes: Jan: rainy month, about 25 rain days. Mornings are often clearer; carry a rain jacket.
Feb: similar to Jan, wet with mild days around 17°C. Pack layers.
Mar: the wettest month, about 29 rain days. Plan indoor sights and short walks.
Apr: still wet, around 28 rain days. Showers are common in the afternoon.
May: rain eases a little, about 25 rain days. Cool nights near 8°C.
Jun: drier, about 18 rain days. Good month for views and hikes.
Jul: one of the driest months, about 12 rain days. Cool nights; bring a warm layer.
Aug: driest and slightly warmer, highs near 19°C. Great for the cable car and day trips.
Sep: still fairly dry, about 15 rain days. Pleasant for walking the old town.
Oct: rain returns, about 25 rain days. Keep plans flexible.
Nov: wet, about 27 rain days. Mornings are your best window.
Dec: wet with about 26 rain days. Mild days, cool nights.

climate_guide.summary: High-altitude equatorial climate: mild all year, cool nights, and rain possible in any month. July to September is driest.

items.title: Rain in most months
items.text: Rain days range from about 12 in July to 29 in March. A light rain jacket beats an umbrella in the wind.

items.title: Mild days, cool nights
items.text: Highs stay near 17–19°C all year; lows are 7–9°C. Bring a warm layer for evenings.

items.title: Best time: July to September
items.text: Fewer rain days and slightly warmer days. Best odds for volcano views and hikes.

items.title: Altitude matters
items.text: Quito sits very high. Take the first day easy, drink water and go slow on stairs.

items.title: Mornings are clearer
items.text: Clouds and showers often build in the afternoon. Do outdoor sights early.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers, a rain jacket, sturdy shoes and sunscreen. The sun is strong at altitude even when cloudy.

transit.best: Metro for main corridors; taxis or apps for short hops and evenings.

modes.text: Runs Quitumbe to El Labrador via Centro Histórico and La Mariscal in about 30 min. Fares $0.45 general, $0.22 reduced. Hours 05:30–23:00 Mon–Fri, 07:00–23:00 Sat, 07:00–22:00 Sun and holidays.
El Trole, Metrobus and Ecovia cost about $0.35 per ride; pay at station entrances.
Yellow taxis with door numbers: day minimum $1, night minimum $2, most city trips under $5. Easy Taxi and Uber work; hotels can call a vetted taxi.
Useful for day trips outside the city. Traffic and parking in the centre are hard; check licence rules.
Best in the old town, which is car-free on Sundays. Watch traffic and take care at altitude.
